title: What is Payment Orchestration? A Technical Primer
summary: Learn how payment orchestration routes transactions across PSPs, where failover breaks, and why reconciliation needs double-entry records.
body_text: Visa Europe showed what single-rail dependency costs on June 1, 2018, when a component within a switch in Visa's primary UK data center suffered a partial failure, preventing the backup switch from activating. The malfunctioning switch created a message backlog that slowed processing at both data centers. The outage lasted roughly 10 hours, during which 5.2 million transactions failed across Europe, including 2.4 million in the UK, leaving merchants on the Visa network with no automatic fallback path. That single point of failure is what payment orchestration is designed to eliminate. What is payment orchestration? Payment orchestration is the layer that, per transaction, decides which payment service provider (PSP) receives the request and what happens when that PSP says no. It turns processor choice from hard-coded application logic into an operational layer that can be inspected, modified, and linked to reconciliation records. Architecturally, payment orchestration depends on four components: 1 Routing logic that selects a PSP per transaction based on configurable rules. 2 PSP connectors that normalize each provider's API into a single internal data model. 3 Reconciliation records that match every orchestrated transaction to its settlement. 4 A double-entry system of record underneath that makes every routing decision auditable. Orchestration controls where a payment goes, but cannot record what happened afterward. Without the fourth component, the routing decision is unreconcilable. A $15,000 charge succeeded somewhere, but the orchestrator cannot tell you which PSP's clearing account holds the funds, or whether the first failed attempt left a residue. How payment orchestration operates in four steps Four steps carry the engineering load of payment orchestration: routing, connector normalization, retry safety, and event-driven flow control. 1. PSP selection and smart routing The routing engine ranks PSPs per transaction inside the payment request path, weighing fixed attributes (BIN, currency, amount, geography, and MCC) against live signals (success rates, fees, fraud flags, PSP health). Cost and acceptance ranking both work at BIN granularity. The biggest gains appear in cross-border routing, where a local acquirer cuts cross-border fees and lifts domestic authorization rates because issuers treat cross-border traffic as higher risk. Most teams start with static rules and add ML models optimizing for approval rate once volume justifies it. 2. Unified connector and API normalization PSP integrations differ in SDKs, API shapes, and HTTP status code handling. A connector framework hides that heterogeneity behind a single internal data model, handling request transformation, response translation, per-provider retry semantics, and circuit breakers. Normalization also covers settlement data; one provider's transaction_id is another's pspReference, and fees may arrive as a single processing_fees or split into interchange_fee, scheme_fee and markup. Mapping everything to a single taxonomy is why later PSP integrations become configuration rather than new codebases. 3. Retry logic, fallback chains, and idempotency Retry correctness is hard because failure is ambiguous. A decline is definitive, but a timeout leaves the outcome unknown, and retrying without an idempotency key that the PSP honors turns a network blip into a double charge. Idempotency guarantees vary by provider (key scope, retention, length limits, and regional behavior), and multi-server deployments without a shared duplicate-check store further weaken the guarantee. Fallback chains define ordered PSPs per region with health-based routing and circuit breakers, because sustained latency spikes and retry storms cascade through dependent services. Every attempt should be traceable as its own object (PSP name, reference, state, normalized error, and timestamps), giving retries a reconcilable history instead of a collapsed status field. 4. Payment flow automation and event-driven triggers Orchestration platforms turn PSP lifecycle transitions into triggers, consuming webhook events through an asynchronous queue so handlers return quickly. Flow builders move coordination out of application code into declarative configuration, chaining steps such as hold funds, await KYC, capture at end-of-day, trigger a payout and write the posting. For multi-step flows across services, the saga pattern is well-suited, as each step publishes an event that triggers the next, with compensating transactions rolling back on failure. When the sequence changes, you edit a flow definition instead of redeploying three services. Four layers of a production payment orchestration stack A production orchestration stack separates four responsibilities to stay auditable: Connectivity, Routing, Reconciliation, and Ledger. We call this the CRRL stack . The top two layers move money while the bottom two prove where it went. 1. Connectivity adapters that normalize PSP APIs Connectivity adapters translate each PSP's proprietary request and response schema into a single internal data model. The adapter normalizes PSP-specific account, payment, and settlement data into a common internal model before writing ledger postings, so product code never sees the raw rail format. Adding a rail changes only the adapter; the checkout flow stays untouched. Adapters are also where reconciliation bugs hide. When a PSP changes a file format or status code, the adapter quietly mismaps a field , and the mismap only surfaces when balances stop matching. Isolating each PSP behind its own adapter keeps schema changes localized. 2. Routing and logic engine for waterfall and retry rules The routing and logic layer houses the rules engine, where waterfall sequences, geographic split ratios, A/B PSP tests, and retry policies reside. Version control safeguards production. For auditability, teams should store a reference to the rule version used for every transaction, along with the decline codes, the PSP and merchant account that handled the attempt, and the legal entity. Without version-controlled rule references, you cannot explain last month's routing decisions to an auditor. 3. Reconciliation across PSPs and bank settlements The reconciliation layer ties each orchestrated transaction to its settlement record from each PSP and detects drift when PSP settlement reports diverge from internal records. The reconciliation topology is often asymmetric: incoming payments reconcile 1:1 on the first leg (order to PSP, by transaction reference), then N:1 on the second leg, where many PSP transactions map to one settlement credit at the bank. 4. Core ledger as the double-entry system of record The core ledger is the double-entry system of record that makes routed transactions auditable through retries and settlement, and represents reversals as new balancing entries. Numscript, Formance's language for financial transactions , expresses a gross-to-net settlement as one atomic multi-posting. Take this example of a $10,000.00 card settlement netting $9,700.00 after $120.00 markup, $50.00 scheme fees, and $130.00 interchange: // CARD_SETTLEMENT // Event: record a $10,000.00 card settlement net of markup, scheme, and interchange fees send [USD/2 1000000] ( source = @counterparties:acquirers:a allowing unbounded overdraft destination = { 970000/1000000 to @merchants:acme:available 12000/1000000 to @platform:expenses:fees:markup 5000/1000000 to @platform:expenses:fees:scheme 13000/1000000 to @platform:expenses:fees:interchange } ) set_tx_meta ( "event_type" , "card_settlement" ) set_tx_meta ( "settlement_id" , "set001" ) All four postings are committed together or not at all, so the fee is preserved per transaction rather than buried in a PSP invoice. The other three layers depend on the core ledger as routing writes intent, connectivity writes PSP events, and reconciliation compares against external reality. Why single-PSP payment stacks break at scale A single-PSP payment stack breaks for structural reasons: vendor concentration, integration sprawl per rail added, and routing decisions scattered across application code. Vendor availability becomes your revenue ceiling If the PSP goes down, rate-limits traffic, or declines a geography-specific segment, the stack has no alternative route and limited visibility into the cause. Every outage window, regional decline pattern, and unannounced rate limit reaches checkout unfiltered. There is no fallback path and no operational lever to pull while the incident is live. Every added rail brings its own schema, webhooks, and settlement format Each added PSP or payment method, including buy now, pay later (BNPL) providers and local payment methods , brings its own request schema, webhook semantics, and settlement report format. Each addition creates a separate data model and reconciliation process, and integration work grows disproportionately as your team maintains a bespoke translation layer for each provider. Routing decisions scatter across application code with no audit trail Without a central routing layer, "which PSP handles this transaction" is determined by application code, spread across checkout logic, retry handlers, and per-region branches. There is no central place where the rule is defined or audited, no way to change it without a deploy, and no reliable answer when an auditor asks why a specific transaction went to a specific processor last month. What new failure modes does orchestration introduce Adding orchestration resolves single-PSP failures but introduces new ones: partial-capture risk after failover, reconciliation drift at high transaction volumes, and broken network token portability. Partial-capture risk after failover Partial-capture risk arises when an authorization succeeds at PSP A, the connection drops before the response reaches PSP A, and the capture routes to PSP B. A ghost authorization now sits open at PSP A: the customer's issuer holds funds against the authorization, the customer can be charged twice, and the reconciliation record never closes cleanly. Partial-capture exposure widens across geography. If a retry routes to a different data center during a regional failover, the idempotency state may need to be visible across processing locations to reduce the risk of duplicate charges. Failover logic should also avoid assuming uniform capture semantics across processors and instruments. Reconciliation drift compounds at high transaction volume Small per-transaction discrepancies across PSPs compound as volume rises. A 0.1% per-transaction discrepancy across three acquirers becomes a five-figure month-end exception queue; each unresolved line blocks the settlement close. Timing differences across acquirers and later refund or chargeback events make those exceptions harder to trace. Reconcile at the transaction level rather than in daily batches. Batch reconciliation surfaces the drift only after it has compounded. Network token portability across PSPs Network token portability breaks when teams using processor vaults try to move volume across PSPs. Re-tokenizing cardholder data creates migration work and may require customers to re-enter payment details. Network-level tokens can reduce processor-vault lock-in when the relevant issuer, network, acquirer, and processor support the token flow. However, support and performance still vary by issuer, processor, and transaction context. Five signals your architecture needs payment orchestration Five signals confirm that you need payment orchestration within your financial architecture: manual multi-PSP routing, geographic authorization variance, single-PSP outage exposure, cross-border expansion, and inconsistent retry logic. 1. You route across three or more PSPs manually in the application code Routing rules embedded in if statements require a code deployment for every change, and the operational drag compounds as the number of providers and payment methods grows. If your PSP count has moved beyond a simple primary-and-backup setup, hand-rolled routing is already the bottleneck. 2. Your authorization rate varies by geography or card network, and nothing exploits that variance A blended authorization rate can hide strong domestic debit performance and weak international credit performance. Local acquiring can help narrow the gap in some cases. Without signal-based routing, that variance is a report you read. 3. A single PSP outage takes your payment stack down Partial outages can affect a specific region, rail, or payment method rather than the entire provider. You cannot integrate your way out mid-incident; onboarding a new acquirer directly can take many months. 4. You are expanding into markets where no single PSP has strong local acquiring coverage Cross-border expansion introduces differences in authentication, acquisition, currency, and compliance across markets. Multi-market coverage means multi-acquirer by construction, and multi-acquirer without orchestration means one bespoke integration per market. 5. Your retry logic is bespoke, inconsistently idempotent, and owned by whoever wrote the original integration Each direct PSP integration carries its own retry implementation with its own assumptions about key retention, scopes, and timeout semantics. Centralizing the taxonomy can reduce duplicated engineering work, as multi-PSP fallbacks may recover transactions that would otherwise fail. Adopting a programmable core ledger beneath the payment orchestrator A programmable core ledger beneath the orchestrator records every fund movement the orchestrator triggers and makes those movements auditable across PSPs. An orchestration platform routes payment instructions: a programmable core ledger records the resulting fund movements, while a reconciliation layer compares them with external statements across connected rails. If you collapse the orchestrator and the ledger into one layer, external PSP APIs become your source of financial truth by default, which is exactly the failure mode a separate ledger prevents.

title: Ascent Industries Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results; Year-Over-Year Net Sales Increase 37.6% and Adjusted EBITDA Improves by $1.8 Million
summary: Sequentially, legacy net sales increased approximately 22% and gross margin expanded approximately 710 basis points; Midwest Graphic Sales…...
body_text: Ascent Industries Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results; Year-Over-Year Net Sales Increase 37.6% and Adjusted EBITDA Improves by $1.8 Million August 04, 2026 4:05pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q Filing PDF HTML XBRL ZIP HTML Sequentially, legacy net sales increased approximately 22% and gross margin expanded approximately 710 basis points; Midwest Graphic Sales was immediately accretive to Adjusted EBITDA. SCHAUMBURG, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Ascent Industries Co. (Nasdaq: ACNT) (“Ascent” or the “Company”), a specialty chemicals platform delivering differentiated, performance-driven chemical solutions, is reporting its results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Summary 1 (in millions, except per share and margin) Q2 2026 Q2 2025 Change Net Sales $25.7 $18.7 37.6% Gross Profit $5.5 $4.9 14.0% Gross Profit Margin 21.6% 26.1% -447bps Net Income (Loss) $0.7 $(2.4) 127.4% Diluted Income (Loss) per Share $0.07 $(0.25) 129.3% Adjusted EBITDA $1.5 $(0.3) +$1.8M Adjusted EBITDA Margin 5.7% (1.8)% +745bps _________________________ 1On May 4, 2026, the Company closed on a transaction to acquire substantially all of the assets of Midwest Graphic Sales, Inc and Sigma Coatings, Inc. (together "Midwest"). The second quarter of 2026 included $1.9 million in net sales, no net income and $0.3 million in Adjusted EBITDA from the acquisition of Midwest. Management Commentary “The second quarter was one of the strongest in our recent history, reflecting continued improvement across the business,” said J. Bryan Kitchen, President and Chief Executive Officer of Ascent Industries Co. “Sequentially, legacy net sales increased approximately 22% and gross margin expanded approximately 710 basis points, while volume, average selling price, gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA also improved. Despite a specialty chemicals market that remains soft, year over year net sales increased approximately 28%, total gross profit increased 14%, and Adjusted EBITDA improved by $1.8 million. On a trailing-twelve-month basis, the company saw record highs for volume, net sales, gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations.” "The sequential improvement in gross margin demonstrates that our optimization initiatives are beginning to translate growth into stronger earnings," Kitchen added. "Although gross margin remains below both the prior-year level and our long-term expectations, our priorities remain unchanged. Commercial execution is creating profitable growth opportunities, while our operations teams apply the same standardize, simplify and optimize playbook that transformed our operating foundation over the past two years. Growth creates the opportunity. Optimization converts that opportunity into earnings. As reported last quarter, our platform-wide optimization initiative remains on track to achieve a run-rate improvement of approximately $3 million to $5 million in annualized gross profit improvement by the end of 2026. As we continue to grow, each operational improvement expands the earnings power of the platform and compounds long-term shareholder returns." “The successful integration of the Midwest Graphic Sales acquisition further reinforces our disciplined acquisition strategy,” Kitchen continued. “In the first two months since we closed, the business performed in line with our expectations, positively contributing to gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA. Back-office integration was completed a full quarter ahead of our original commitment, the manufacturing transition remains on schedule, and our teams are already developing opportunities beyond the original underwriting case. We are building a combined business that is more capable and more valuable than either company could have become independently.” Kitchen concluded, “Our strategy remains unchanged. What has changed is the evidence that it is delivering the outcomes we envisioned. Over the past two years, we have systematically improved the quality of our portfolio, strengthened our commercial execution, enhanced our operational excellence and applied disciplined capital allocation. Together, these capabilities are reinforcing one another, creating a higher-quality business capable of delivering consistent growth, higher returns on invested capital and greater long-term shareholder value across market cycles.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Net sales from continuing operations were $25.7 million compared to $18.7 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase was a result of increases in volume and average selling prices. Gross profit from continuing operations increased 14.0% to $5.5 million, or 21.6% of net sales, compared to $4.9 million, or 26.1% of net sales, in the second quarter of 2025. The increase in dollars was primarily driven by increases in cost recovery in the period due to increased production, reductions in utilities, and repairs and maintenance partially offset by increases in labor and overhead. Net income from continuing operations increased to $0.7 million compared to a net loss of ($2.4) million in the second quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share increased to $0.07 in the second quarter of 2026 compared to a diluted loss per share of ($0.25) in the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations increased to $1.5 million in the second quarter of 2026, with adjusted EBITDA margin increasing to 5.7% compared to (1.8)% in the prior year period. The increase was primarily driven by the aforementioned increase in gross profit as well as reductions in SG&A in the current year. Liquidity As of June 30, 2026, the Company had $28.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, no debt outstanding under its revolving credit facilities and had $17.9 million in availability under its revolving credit facility. For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 209,868 shares at an average cost of $13.80 per share for approximately $2.9 million. Conference Call Ascent will hold a conference call today at 5:00 p.m. Eastern time to discuss its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Ascent management will host the conference call, followed by a question-and-answer period. An operator will register your name and organization. If you have any difficulty connecting with the conference call, please contact Investor Relations at 1-630-884-9181. The conference call will also be broadcast live and available for replay via the webcast registration link above. The webcast will be archived for one year in the investor relations section of the Company’s website at www.ascentco.com . About Ascent Industries Co. Ascent Industries Co. title: Enhancing Customs Operations Through Visibility, Reporting, and Analytics
summary: Learn how EXP.O NOW enhances customs operations with improved visibility, reporting, and analytics for effective compliance and decision-making.
body_text: For Customs and Compliance teams, staying on top of import activity requires greater visibility and control than ever before. Customs and Compliance professionals are expected to monitor declarations in progress, understand the financial impact of tariffs and duties, prepare stakeholder reports, and support compliance requirements, often while managing large volumes of data across multiple systems. These responsibilities can create operational challenges that affect visibility, decision-making, and day-to-day efficiency. Through customer feedback and industry engagement, Expeditors has identified several common pain points faced by Customs and Compliance teams: Limited visibility into declaration status and potential delays Difficulty understanding tariff and duty impacts Time-consuming reporting and audit preparation Increasing compliance requirements and oversight responsibilities While every organization faces unique challenges, these issues consistently impact the ability of Customs and Compliance teams to make informed decisions, respond quickly to disruptions, and maintain confidence in their customs operations. Addressing Customer Challenges Through EXP.O NOW To help address these challenges, Expeditors continues to enhance EXP.O NOW with solutions designed to improve visibility, simplify reporting, support analysis of import tariffs and duties, and strengthen compliance oversight. Declarations by Status Panel - The Declarations by Status Panel gives Customs and Compliance teams a real-time view of declaration progress throughout the clearance process. By bringing status updates into a single dashboard, customers can quickly identify declarations that require attention or may be at risk of delays. This visibility helps teams respond proactively, improve operational efficiency, and keep goods moving as planned. EXP.O NOW Tariff Calculator - The Tariff Calculator helps users understand U.S. duty rates and the financial impact of trade actions on imported goods. Organizations can compare U.S. duty costs across countries of origin, evaluate sourcing options, and improve import forecasting. By identifying applicable U.S. duties and tariffs in advance, the tool supports more informed decisions, greater cost visibility, and stronger compliance planning. EXP.O NOW Visibility Reports - Visibility Reports provide on-demand access to customs data through self-service and scheduled reporting capabilities. Customers can easily access declaration and invoice-level details to support internal analysis, compliance reviews, and audit preparation. By centralizing key customs information, Visibility Reports help improve oversight and enable more confident decision-making. EXP.O NOW Analytics - EXP.O NOW Analytics provides dashboard-driven insights across Transportation, Customs Brokerage, and Order Management data. Through Brokerage Timing Analysis and Duty Recovery Analysis, customers can identify process inefficiencies, evaluate performance, uncover duty recovery opportunities, and track refund progress. By bringing operational and financial insights together in one place, Analytics helps customers make more informed decisions and optimize customs performance. Across visibility, reporting, tariff and duty management, and analytics, Expeditors continues to enhance EXP.O NOW with capabilities designed to support Customs and Compliance operations. By providing greater access to data, insights, and self-service tools, EXP.O NOW improves visibility, strengthens compliance efforts, and supports more informed decision-making. Expeditors remains committed to delivering solutions that provide greater efficiency, transparency, and control across customs operations. If you're looking for support managing your supply chain and navigating customs compliance, reach out to your local Expeditors representative to learn more about the EXP.O NOW platform and its capabilities.

body_text: Star Group, L.P. Reports Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results August 5, 2026 PDF Version STAMFORD, Conn., Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Star Group, L.P. (the "Company" or "Star") (NYSE:SGU), a home energy distributor and services provider, today filed its quarterly report on Form 10-Q with the SEC and announced financial results for the fiscal 2026 third quarter, the three months ended June 30, 2026. Three Months Ended June 30, 2026 Compared to the Three Months Ended June 30, 2025 For the fiscal 2026 third quarter, Star reported a 17.2 percent increase in total revenue to $358.1 million compared with $305.6 million in the prior-year period, reflecting an increase in average selling prices, driven by higher wholesale product cost. The amount of home heating oil and propane sold during the fiscal 2026 third quarter declined by 3.4 million gallons, or 9.4 percent, to 32.8 million gallons, as the additional volume provided from acquisitions and colder temperatures was more than offset by the impact of net customer attrition and other factors. Temperatures in Star's geographic areas of operation for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were 15.9 percent colder than the three months ended June 30, 2025 but 5.9 percent warmer than normal, as reported by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Star’s net loss rose by $11.4 million in the quarter, to $28.0 million, primarily due to an unfavorable change in the fair value of derivative instruments of $8.6 million and a $7.1 million increase in Adjusted EBITDA loss, partially offset by a $3.4 million increase in the Company’s income tax benefit and a $0.9 million decrease in depreciation and amortization expenses. The Company reported a third quarter Adjusted EBITDA loss (a non-GAAP measure defined below) of $17.7 million, up $7.1 million year-over-year, as higher home heating oil and propane per gallon margins, an improvement in service and installation profitability and the additional gross profit from other petroleum products were more than offset by higher operating expenses, including $6.2 million in higher insurance-related expenses, and the lower volume of home heating oil and propane sold. “Our results this quarter, a non-heating period, largely reflected seasonal factors and net attrition, which was in line with prior-year periods” said Jeff Woosnam, Star Group’s President and Chief Executive Officer. “While temperatures were moderately colder than last year, the volume of home heating oil and propane sold was lower given the more muted impact of additional degree days in the shoulder months of April and May. We did not complete any acquisitions this quarter but are actively assessing a number of possible attractive opportunities. We are taking steps this summer, as in years past, to improve our operations, streamline where appropriate, and prepare for the coming winter months. At the same time, we continue to invest in our service and installation business – where we see further room for growth – and believe Star remains in great shape for the quarters to come.” Nine Months Ended June 30, 2026 Compared to the Nine Months Ended June 30, 2025 For the nine months ended June 30, 2026, Star reported an 8.3 percent increase in total revenue to $1.7 billion, reflecting higher product volumes sold and an increase in selling prices in response to higher wholesale product costs. The volume of home heating oil and propane sold during the first nine months of fiscal 2026 increased by 8.6 million gallons, or 3.3 percent, to 271.2 million gallons, reflecting colder temperatures and the additional volume provided from acquisitions, more than offsetting net customer attrition and other factors. Temperatures in Star’s geographic areas of operation fiscal year-to-date were 11.5 percent colder than during the prior-year period and 2.9 percent colder than normal, as reported by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. For the nine months ended June 30, 2026, Star’s net income increased $13.9 million, to $116.1 million, compared to the prior-year period, primarily due to a $19.9 million increase in Adjusted EBITDA, a favorable change in the fair value of derivative instruments of $1.4 million, and a $0.6 million decrease in depreciation and amortization expenses, partially offset by a $7.6 million increase in income taxes and $0.4 million higher net interest expense. Year-to-date Adjusted EBITDA increased $19.9 million, to $189.3 million, compared to the nine months ended June 30, 2025, primarily due to an increase in home heating oil and propane per gallon margins and volume sold in the base business, and an increase in Adjusted EBITDA from acquisitions, which more than offset higher operating expenses, of which $1.9 million was attributable to the Company's weather hedge contracts due to colder weather. The temperatures experienced during the weather hedge period ending March 31, 2026 were colder than in the prior-year period and, therefore, the Company recorded an expense under the weather hedge contracts of $5.0 million in fiscal 2026 versus a $3.1 million expense recorded in fiscal 2025. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA (Non-GAAP Financial Measures) EBITDA (Earnings from continuing operations before net interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization) and Adjusted EBITDA (Earnings from continuing operations before net interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, (increase) decrease in the fair value of derivatives, other income (loss), net, multiemployer pension plan withdrawal charge, gain or loss on debt redemption, goodwill impairment, and other non-cash and non-operating charges) are non-GAAP financial measures that are used as supplemental financial measures by management and external users of the Company’s financial statements, such as investors, commercial banks and research analysts, to assess Star’s position with regard to the following: compliance with certain financial covenants included in our debt agreements; financial performance without regard to financing methods, capital structure, income taxes or historical cost basis; operating performance and return on invested capital compared to those of other companies in the retail distribution of refined petroleum products, without regard to financing methods and capital structure; ability to generate cash sufficient to pay interest on our indebtedness and to make distributions to our partners; and the viability of acquisitions and capital expenditure projects and the overall rates of return of alternative investment opportunities. The method of calculating Adjusted EBITDA may not be consistent with that of other companies, and EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA both have limitations as analytical tools and so should not be viewed in isolation but in conjunction with measurements that are computed in accordance with GAAP. Some of the limitations of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are as follows: EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect cash used for capital expenditures; although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated or amortized often will have to be replaced and EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect the cash requirements for such replacements; EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, working capital; EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect the cash necessary to make payments of interest or principal on indebtedness; and EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect the cash required to pay taxes. REMINDER: Members of Star's management team will host a webcast and conference call at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time tomorrow, August 6, 2026. The webcast will be accessible on the company’s website, at www.stargrouplp.com , and the telephone number for the conference call is 888-346-3470 (or 412-317-5169 for international callers). About Star Group, L.P. Star Group, L.P. is a full service provider specializing in the sale of home heating products and services to residential and commercial customers to heat their homes and buildings. The Company also sells and services heating and air conditioning equipment to its home heating oil and propane customers and, to a lesser extent, provides these offerings to customers outside of its home heating oil and propane customer base. Star also sells diesel, gasoline and home heating oil on a delivery only basis. We believe Star is the nation's largest retail distributor of home heating oil based upon sales volume. Including its propane locations, Star serves customers in the more northern and eastern states within the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic U.S. regions. Additional information is available by obtaining the Company's SEC filings at www.sec.gov and by visiting Star's website at www.stargrouplp.com , where unit holders may request a hard copy of Star’s complete audited financial statements free of charge. title: ¿Cómo quitar uñas acrílicas en casa sin dañar tus uñas? Guía paso a paso
summary: Aprende cómo quitar uñas acrílicas en casa sin dañar tus uñas naturales, paso a paso, y agenda tu retiro y manicure profesional a domicilio con Glitzi.
body_text: ¿Tus uñas acrílicas ya crecieron demasiado, comenzaron a levantarse o simplemente quieres cambiar de diseño? Probablemente lo primero que buscaste fue cómo quitar uñas acrílicas en casa sin dañar tus uñas naturales . Y aquí viene la regla más importante: no las jales ni intentes arrancarlas. Aunque puede parecer la forma más rápida de retirarlas, hacerlo puede llevarse también capas de tu uña natural y dejarla delgada, sensible o debilitada. La buena noticia es que existen formas mucho más cuidadosas de remover uñas acrílicas en casa . En esta guía te explicamos cómo hacerlo paso a paso, qué errores debes evitar y cuándo es mejor dejar el retiro en manos de una profesional. ¿Se pueden quitar las uñas acrílicas en casa? Sí, pero necesitas hacerlo con paciencia y utilizando los materiales adecuados. Las uñas acrílicas están diseñadas para adherirse firmemente a la uña natural. Por eso, intentar levantarlas, despegarlas o arrancarlas puede dañar su superficie. El objetivo de un buen retiro no es simplemente eliminar el acrílico: es hacerlo protegiendo lo más posible tu uña natural . Si no tienes los materiales necesarios, tus uñas están muy adheridas o simplemente prefieres evitar el proceso, también puedes optar por un retiro de uñas profesional a domicilio . ¿Qué necesitas para quitar uñas acrílicas en casa? Antes de comenzar, prepara todo lo necesario para evitar interrupciones durante el proceso. Vas a necesitar: Cortauñas. Lima de uñas. Acetona pura. Algodón. Papel aluminio. Empujador de cutícula o palito de naranjo. Buffer o lima pulidora suave. Aceite para cutícula. Crema hidratante para manos. Y algo muy importante: tiempo . Uno de los errores más comunes al retirar uñas postizas en casa es querer acelerar el proceso cuando el acrílico todavía sigue adherido. Si tienes que hacer fuerza para quitarlo, todavía no está listo. Cómo quitar uñas acrílicas en casa paso a paso Paso 1. Reduce el largo de las uñas acrílicas Comienza cortando cuidadosamente el largo de las uñas. Mientras menos producto tengas que remover, más sencillo será el proceso. Hazlo poco a poco y evita cortar demasiado cerca de tu uña natural. Si alguna parte del acrílico está levantada, no aproveches para jalarla: déjala para los siguientes pasos. ‍ Paso 2. Lima la capa superior del acrílico Utiliza una lima para retirar suavemente el brillo y la capa superior del acrílico. Este paso permite que la acetona penetre mejor y ayude a ablandar el producto. No necesitas eliminar todo el acrílico con la lima. De hecho, hacerlo puede terminar dañando tu uña natural. La idea es únicamente retirar el acabado superficial. ‍ Paso 3. Protege la piel alrededor de tus uñas La acetona puede resecar bastante la piel y las cutículas. Antes de continuar, puedes aplicar una pequeña cantidad de vaselina alrededor de cada uña para crear una barrera protectora. Procura no colocarla directamente sobre el acrílico, ya que necesitamos que la acetona pueda actuar sobre él. Paso 4. Coloca algodón con acetona Empapa pequeños trozos de algodón con acetona pura y coloca uno sobre cada uña. Después, envuelve cuidadosamente cada dedo con papel aluminio. Esto ayuda a mantener el algodón en contacto con el acrílico y evita que la acetona se evapore demasiado rápido. Déjalo actuar aproximadamente 20 a 30 minutos . El tiempo puede variar dependiendo del grosor del acrílico y del producto que hayan utilizado en tus uñas. ‍ Paso 5. Revisa si el acrílico ya se desprende Retira el papel aluminio de una sola uña para comprobar el resultado. El acrílico debería verse mucho más suave y comenzar a desprenderse fácilmente. Utiliza un empujador de cutícula o palito de naranjo para retirar el producto con movimientos suaves. ¿Tienes que hacer fuerza? No lo jales. Vuelve a colocar algodón con acetona y déjalo actuar unos minutos más. Forzar el acrílico puede retirar también capas superficiales de tu uña natural. Paso 6. Elimina los pequeños restos de producto Una vez que hayas retirado la mayor parte del acrílico, puedes utilizar un buffer suave para eliminar los pequeños restos que hayan quedado. Hazlo delicadamente. No necesitas pulir hasta sentir la uña completamente lisa. Limar demasiado puede adelgazarla y dejarla sensible. Paso 7. Hidrata tus uñas y cutículas Después de utilizar acetona, este paso es indispensable. Aplica aceite para cutícula alrededor de cada uña y masajea suavemente. Después utiliza una crema hidratante en manos y dedos. Puedes repetir este ritual durante los siguientes días para mantener tus uñas y cutículas hidratadas. ‍ Lo que NUNCA debes hacer para quitar uñas acrílicas Sabemos que es tentador. Una esquina comienza a levantarse y automáticamente dan ganas de jalarla hasta retirar toda la uña. Pero este es precisamente uno de los errores que más pueden dañar tus uñas naturales. Cuando arrancas el acrílico, también puedes retirar capas de queratina de la superficie de la uña. Por eso, evita: Jalar o arrancar el acrílico. Introducir objetos debajo de la uña para despegarlo. Morder las uñas postizas. Raspar agresivamente la superficie. Limar hasta adelgazar la uña natural. Intentar acelerar el proceso haciendo fuerza. Si el producto no se desprende fácilmente, necesita más tiempo. ¿Por qué las uñas pueden quedar débiles después de retirar el acrílico? Existe la idea de que usar uñas acrílicas inevitablemente destruye las uñas naturales, pero muchas veces el verdadero problema está en cómo se aplican y, especialmente, cómo se retiran . Un limado excesivo, jalar el acrílico o raspar demasiado la superficie puede debilitar la uña. Además, después del retiro puedes sentir tus uñas mucho más delgadas simplemente porque estabas acostumbrada al grosor y dureza del acrílico. Por eso, el cuidado posterior es tan importante como el retiro. Cómo cuidar tus uñas después de retirar el acrílico Después de remover tus uñas acrílicas , dale un poco de atención extra a tus manos. Durante los siguientes días procura mantener tus uñas cortas y aplica aceite de cutícula diariamente. También puedes: Utilizar crema hidratante después de lavarte las manos. Evitar limar excesivamente la superficie. Darle unos días de descanso a tus uñas si están sensibles. Utilizar guantes cuando limpies o tengas contacto prolongado con agua. Hacerte un manicure para recuperar forma, hidratación y una apariencia cuidada. Si notas dolor persistente, inflamación, cambios importantes de color o señales de infección, evita colocar nuevamente uñas postizas y consulta con un profesional de salud. ¿Es mejor quitar uñas acrílicas en casa o hacer un retiro profesional? Depende del estado de tus uñas. Puedes quitar uñas acrílicas en casa si tienes los materiales adecuados, suficiente tiempo y puedes hacerlo con paciencia. Sin embargo, un retiro profesional puede ser una mejor opción cuando: El acrílico está demasiado adherido. Tienes varias capas de producto. No sabes exactamente qué producto utilizaron. Alguna uña está lastimada. Tus uñas naturales ya están débiles. Simplemente no quieres pasar 30, 40 o más minutos retirando producto. Además, puedes aprovechar la misma cita para hacerte un manicure y dejar tus uñas naturales cuidadas después del retiro. Retiro de uñas y manicure sin salir de casa Si llegaste hasta aquí buscando cómo quitar uñas acrílicas en casa , hay una alternativa todavía más cómoda: dejar que una profesional se encargue sin que tú tengas que ir al salón. Con Glitzi puedes agendar servicios de uñas a domicilio y recibir a una coach directamente en tu casa. Puedes combinar tu retiro con un manicure para consentir tus manos, cuidar tus uñas naturales y dejarlas listas para su próximo diseño… o simplemente disfrutar de unas uñas naturales y cuidadas. Sin tráfico. Sin filas. Sin perder tiempo yendo al salón. Tus uñas naturales también merecen un poco de amor Cambiar de diseño, descansar del acrílico o regresar a una manicure natural no debería significar sacrificar la salud y apariencia de tus uñas. Recuerda la regla de oro: si el acrílico no sale fácilmente, no lo jales. Haz el retiro con paciencia o déjalo en manos de una profesional. ¿Prefieres olvidarte del proceso? Agenda un retiro de uñas y manicure profesional con Glitzi a domicilio. Tu coach llega hasta tu casa para consentir tus manos y dejar tus uñas listas para su siguiente etapa.

title: Why won't consumers stop spending?
summary: Inflation doesn't appear to be slowing overall consumer spending and stable employment is one reason why
body_text: Always problematic for bond investors, inflation’s return to the front pages this decade has been increasingly framed as the consumer's chief nemesis. Prices are higher, borrowing costs have increased, and many households continue to express frustration about the cost of everyday necessities. Yet consumer spending remains remarkably resilient. Are observers focusing on the price side of the equation and overlooking the income side? We know that consumers may not make spending decisions based solely on what things cost—they often make decisions based on how confident they feel about earning a paycheck tomorrow. And while inflation remains uncomfortable in the post-Covid era, the labor market continues to provide a level of security that was absent during much of the period between the Global Financial Crisis and the pandemic. The recent inflation-employment dynamic From 2007 through 2020, core inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) averaged just 1.6% annually. On the surface, that sounds like an ideal backdrop for consumers. Prices were relatively stable and purchasing power faced fewer headwinds than it does today. The challenge was that job security often felt far less certain. For consumers aged 25-34—a key spending cohort—the unemployment rate averaged 5.4% during that period and peaked near 9% in 2009. Labor-force participation hovered around 77%, spending considerable time closer to 75%. The quits rate told a similar story. Between 2009 and 2012, the rate sat at or below 1.5%, indicating workers were generally reluctant to leave an existing job. Few people voluntarily quit when unsure where the next opportunity will come from. In other words, prices were known, but income prospects were less certain. Consumers may have faced less inflation, but caution often prevailed because the consequences of losing a job felt significant. Pandemic to present: higher inflation, better prospects The last several years have brought a very different set of circumstances. Inflation surged to 5% in 2022, declined to 4% in 2023, and settled around 3% in subsequent years. Despite significant progress from the peak, inflation remains above the levels many consumers grew accustomed to prior to the pandemic. Tariffs, energy costs, and other supply-side pressures have also made a sustained return to 2% inflation difficult. So why has spending remained resilient? One explanation is that consumers continue to view the job market as relatively healthy. For the 25-34 age cohort, unemployment recently stood at 3.7%, below the long-term average of 4.8% since 2000. Labor-force participation has remained above 80%, noticeably stronger than during much of the 2007-2019 period. The quits rate, while down from its 2021 peak near 3%, remains around its long-term average. Workers are still willing to leave jobs voluntarily, suggesting confidence in their ability to find new opportunities. Are consumers adapting? Consumers may not like higher prices, but they are generally more willing to absorb them when they believe their income stream is secure. A worker who expects to remain employed—or perhaps secure a better job—approaches spending decisions differently than one worried about layoffs or stagnant opportunities. None of this means consumers have become indifferent to inflation. Instead, they may have become more selective. We know that technology has made comparison shopping easier than ever. Consumers are better able to evaluate prices across retailers, compare products, and seek alternatives. Value has become increasingly important, but value is not synonymous with the lowest price. In grocery stores, consumers regularly choose among premium, private-label, organic, convenience-oriented, and budget options. Similar dynamics play out across apparel, travel, fitness, and entertainment. Lifestyle preferences also increasingly influence purchasing decisions. Health, wellness, convenience, and personal identity often compete with price as drivers of consumption. Winners and losers across industries Companies that deliver a compelling value proposition—whether through price, quality, convenience, health benefits, or brand appeal—continue to capture consumer dollars. Those that fail to justify their place in the household budget are finding it harder to compete. For bond investors, the key takeaway is that inflation alone may not be sufficient to derail consumer activity. As long as employment conditions remain healthy and workers retain confidence in their ability to generate income, spending can remain more resilient than traditional inflation-focused narratives might suggest. The challenge is that resilience is unlikely to be distributed evenly across the economy. This environment reinforces the value of active management and fundamental research. Consumers are increasingly selective with their spending, rewarding companies that can clearly demonstrate value—whether through price, quality, convenience, innovation, or brand strength—while penalizing those that struggle to differentiate themselves. The result is a wider dispersion between potential winners and losers across industries. At the same time, forecasting inflation remains difficult. While pandemic-related supply disruptions have largely faded, new influences—including tariffs, energy price volatility, geopolitical developments, and substantial AI-related capital spending—have introduced fresh uncertainty into the inflation outlook. Rather than a straight path lower, inflation may continue to follow a more uneven trajectory that keeps both consumers and policymakers on alert. Against that backdrop, we believe the Federal Reserve is likely to remain patient until clearer evidence emerges that inflation is either sustainably moderating or reaccelerating. For fixed income investors, this argues against reaching aggressively for risk. Instead, an emphasis on high-quality securities, disciplined sector selection, and a short duration profile continues to offer an attractive balance between income generation and risk management. More broadly, a market characterized by resilient consumers, uneven inflation, and heightened policy uncertainty should create an environment where selectivity matters—and where active investors can be well positioned to capitalize on opportunities as they emerge. title: 7 Best Lip Balm for Dry Lips Suggested By Dermatologists
summary: Tired of painful, peeling chapped lips? Find 7 dermatologist-recommended lip balms for dry lips that lock in deep hydration, and restore your smile.
body_text: Roles of Lip Balm for Dry Lips Best Lip Balm for Dry Lips Lip Balm Ingredients for Dry Lips Deriving Maximum Benefits from Lip Balm FAQs Ever tried applying your favorite lipstick, only to have it highlight every single dry, peeling flake? Chapped lips are more than just an annoyance; they can make simple things like smiling, eating, or drinking a hot cup of coffee downright painful. Harsh winds, dry air, and sun exposure constantly strip away your lips' delicate moisture, leaving them cracked, stinging, and impossible to soothe with basic hydrators. The fix? You need a deeply nourishing Lip Balm for dry lips. Packed with powerful ceramides, rich natural butters, and protective SPF, the right balm instantly seals in moisture, repairs damaged skin barriers, and restores a soft, healthy smile. In this writeup, we’ll discuss the role of these lip products, and find out dermatologists recommended lip balms for dry lips. How Lip Balm Protects Your Dry Lips Unlike the rest of your skin, the skin on your lips is uniquely fragile. It lacks oil glands (sebaceous glands) and has a significantly thinner stratum corneum, making it ill-equipped to retain moisture or defend itself against harsh environmental factors. Adding a lip balm for cracked lips acts as an artificial support system, using a combination of targeted dermatological mechanisms to restore and protect dry lips. 1. Lock in Moisture with Occlusive Barriers The primary function of lip balm is preventing Transepidermal Water Loss (TEWL). Lip balms utilize powerful occlusive agents; such as beeswax, petrolatum, dimethicone, or plant waxes, that form a physical, hydrophobic barrier over the surface. This barrier seals in existing hydration and stops ambient dry air, wind, and low humidity from evaporating moisture out of your lips. 2. Deeply Hydrate with Humectants To treat deep-seated dryness, high-performance formulations include humectants like hyaluronic acid, glycerin, and panthenol. These active molecules act as moisture magnets, actively pulling water from the deeper layers of your dermis (and the surrounding humidity) directly into the outer layers of the lip tissue, instantly plumping and softening dry flakes. 3. Rebuild and Repair the Skin Barrier When lips become severely chapped, their microscopic lipid barrier breaks down, causing inflammation, peeling, and stinging. Lip balms designed for chapped lips are often rich in emollient ingredients; such as ceramides, shea butter, plant oils, and Vitamin E, fill the intercellular spaces between damaged skin cells. This replenishes essential fatty acids, repairs structural gaps, and restores smooth skin texture. 4. Shield Against Environmental and UV Damage Excessive sun exposure and thermal stress accelerate lip dryness by degrading collagen and triggering inflammation. Lip balms infused with broad-spectrum mineral or chemical SPF filters, alongside antioxidants, block harmful UVA/UVB rays and neutralize free radicals. This prevents solar-induced chapping, dark spots, and long-term tissue damage. Top 7 Lip Balm for Dry Lips: Dermatologists’ Picks Finding the right lip balm in the Indian skincare industry is a tough job. The diversity in the brands, and their marketing gimmicks can confuse you and thus, to ease your search, here are some of the best lip balms for dry lips recommended by dermatologists, offering optimal results. Product Name Key Ingredients Benefits Pecefino Lip Balm Avocado Butter, Beeswax, Tocotrienol (Vitamin E) Intensely moisturizes, repairs cracked skin, and protects against environmental elements with a non-greasy finish. d'you Tender Lip Nectar Camellia Japonica Seed Oil, Candellia Wax, Tocopherol Provides a lightweight balm-oil hybrid formula that heals cracks, locks in hydration, and leaves a non-sticky glossy finish. Sebamed Lip Defense Triple Protection SPF 30 Jojoba Oil, Cera Alba (Beeswax), Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E) Delivers triple protection against UV rays, wind, and dryness while maintaining the skin's natural pH. WishCare Ceramide Lip Balm SPF 50 PA+++ Ceramides (Ceramide NP), Niacinamide, Shea Butter, Tinosorb M Heals severely chapped lips, fades pigmentation, and provides high-level broad-spectrum sun protection. Uriage Bariéderm-Cica Protecting Lip Balm Poly-2P Complex, Squalane, Glycerin, Microcrystalline Wax Creates an insulating, dermatological cica-barrier that soothes, repairs, and protects damaged lips. Essnix Lip Balm SPF 15 Cocoa Butter, Strawberry Butter, Beeswax, Tocopheryl Acetate Deeply nourishes dry lips, repairs chapping, and offers SPF 15 sun protection with a smooth finish. Burt's Beeswax Lip Balm Beeswax, Coconut Oil, Sunflower Seed Oil, Peppermint Oil, Vitamin E Strengthens the natural barrier, locks in long-lasting moisture, and provides a cooling sensation. 1. Pecefino Lip Balm Pecefino Lip Balm is a deeply restorative treatment created to treat chronically dry, rough, and cracked lips. Formulated with rich emollients like avocado butter, coconut oil, and beeswax, it creates a thick protective coating that seals in moisture. The addition of Tocotrienol (a potent form of Vitamin E) accelerates cell repair, helping soothe painful cracking. Dermatologists often recommend butter-and-wax heavy balms like Pecefino because they act as strong occlusives. By forming a durable physical barrier, it stops water from evaporating out of compromised skin tissue, allowing cracked lips to heal without further friction or irritation. Who Should Avoid It Active Acne-Prone Skin Around the Mouth: The rich natural oils and waxes can be comedogenic if applied past the lip line. Nut/Avocado Allergies: Those with severe sensitivities or allergies to avocado or coconut oil should avoid this formula. 2. d'you Tender Lip Nectar This lip balm for chapped lips fulfills the gap between clinical skin repair and everyday beauty aesthetics. Designed as a hybrid balm-oil, it delivers the deep nourishing benefits of traditional balms alongside the lightweight finish of a lip oil. Its formula relies on Ceramide NP and Camellia seed oil to strengthen damaged skin structures while providing a non-sticky glaze. Instead of just coating the surface, it addresses skin health from within by restoring essential lipids through ceramides. Dermatologists praise ceramide-based treatments because they directly rebuild the intercellular matrix of fragile skin, preventing long-term dehydration. Who Should Avoid It Fragrance-Sensitive Skin: Features a subtle Earl Grey tea fragrance, which may irritate individuals with severe contact dermatitis. Budget Shoppers: Positions itself as a premium hybrid treatment, making it less ideal for those looking for basic daily chapsticks. 3. Sebamed Lip Defense Triple Protection SPF 30 It’s considered among one of the best lip balms, known as a specialized pharmacy-grade lip stick designed to hydrate while shielding skin from harsh environmental factors. Formulated at a skin-friendly pH 5.5, it combines jojoba oil, beeswax, and Vitamin E to relieve dry lips while providing SPF 30 broad-spectrum UV protection. It is a go-to dermatologist recommendation for patients taking drying acne treatments (like isotretinoin/Accutane). Its pH 5.5 formulation matches healthy skin, preventing microbial irritation while offering chemical sun filters without a heavy or sticky residue. Who Should Avoid It Chemical Sunscreen Sensitivity: Uses chemical UV filters that may cause a mild stinging sensation on raw, open lip wounds. Overnight Moisture Needs: Best suited for daytime use due to its SPF ingredients. 4. WishCare Ceramide Lip Balm SPF 50 PA+++ This Lip Balm is a multi-action treatment that repairs damaged moisture barriers while protecting against sun-induced hyperpigmentation. It blends Ceramides, Niacinamide, and Kojic Acid with a mix of natural nut oils, hybrid mineral, and chemical UV filters. Dermatologists often highlight this formula for patients suffering from both chapped lips and lip darkening (hyperpigmentation). The combination of Ceramides for barrier repair, SPF 50 for protection, and Niacinamide to fade dark spots makes it a complete daytime lip care routine. Who Should Avoid It Minimalists Wanting Simple Hydration: Active brightening agents like Niacinamide and Kojic Acid may prove unnecessary for those simply seeking basic moisturization. Nighttime Lip Care: High SPF ratings mean it should be washed off before bed rather than used as an overnight sleep mask. 5. Uriage Bariéderm-Cica Protecting Lip Balm This Lip balm for dry lips offers an intensive dermatological lip salve crafted specifically for severely compromised, peeling, or chemically-damaged lips. Using a specialized Poly-2P complex along with squalane and microcrystalline wax, it isolates the lip tissue from irritants while accelerating deep healing. Dermatologists recommend this formula for acute angular cheilitis, eczema flare-ups, and severe weather damage. Its non-perfumed, barrier-building texture acts like a liquid bandage, allowing cracked tissue to regenerate beneath an insulating shield. Who Should Avoid It Gloss Lovers: Focuses entirely on clinical repair rather than cosmetic appearance, leaving a matte-to-semi-matte therapeutic finish. Those Seeking Daily Lightweight Wear: Its heavy, salve-like consistency can feel overly thick for mild everyday dryness. 6. Essnix Lip Balm SPF 15 This affordable everyday lip conditioner is designed to keep lips soft, smooth, and protected from daily sun exposure. Formulated with cocoa butter, strawberry extracts, beeswax, and Vitamin E, it glides smoothly onto the skin to provide immediate moisture and light sun protection. It offers an accessible blend of emollients and broad-spectrum SPF 15 protection. Dermatologists support simple, butter-based formulas like this for daily maintenance, as they prevent everyday environmental chapping without relying on complex active acids. Who Should Avoid It Intense Outdoor Sun Exposure: An SPF 15 rating is insufficient for prolonged, direct sunlight or beach days. Flavored/Scented Balm Sensitivities: The fruit-derived flavorings may entice users to lick their lips, which can worsen dry lips over time. 7. Burt's Beeswax Lip Balm This Lip Balm for chapped lips is a globally recognized, 100% natural formula designed to condition and seal dry lips. Powered by natural beeswax, coconut oil, sunflower seed oil, and a touch of peppermint oil, it creates a firm protective barrier that locks in moisture while leaving a signature cooling sensation. It remains a classic choice due to its high concentration of natural waxes. Dermatologists acknowledge beeswax as one of the most effective natural occlusives available, making this balm an ideal pick for locking in moisture during windy or freezing weather. Who Should Avoid It Sensitive/Reactive Skin: Peppermint oil contains natural menthol, which can trigger a burning sensation, contact dermatitis , or increased dryness in sensitive or severely cracked lips. Vegan Consumers: Contains natural beeswax, making it unsuitable for strictly vegan skincare routines. Dermatologist-Recommended Ingredients for Dry Lips When severe dry skin strikes, not all lip balms are created equal. Dermatologists look for specific, proven active ingredients that work together to restore, hydrate, and shield fragile lip tissue. To effectively treat chapped lips , your balm should feature a blend of three essential ingredient categories: Occlusives (The Moisture Lock): Ingredients like Beeswax , Petrolatum, and Microcrystalline Wax create an invisible physical barrier over your skin. This seals in hydration and prevents wind, dry air, and cold temperatures from stripping away moisture. Humectants (The Water Magnets): Active molecules such as Glycerin, Hyaluronic Acid, and Panthenol pull water deep into the skin's surface layers. They actively attract hydration from the surrounding air to plump and soften tight, dehydrated lips. Emollients & Barrier Repairs (The Skin Healers): Rich natural fats and lipids like Ceramides, Shea Butter, Jojoba Oil, Avocado Butter, and Squalane fill the tiny microscopic cracks between peeling skin cells. They help replenish your natural lipid barrier, relieve stinging, and restore smooth, comfortable skin texture. Protective Antioxidants & Sun Filters: Vitamin E (Tocopherol) helps heal damaged tissue, while broad-spectrum SPF filters (such as Zinc Oxide or Tinosorb) defend fragile lips against UV rays that cause chronic dryness and cracking. How to Apply Lip Balm for Maximum Results Applying lip balm seems straightforward, but a few targeted tweaks can make a massive difference in how effectively it heals and hydrates your lips. Prep on Damp Lips: Apply your balm right after washing your face or showering while your lips are still slightly damp. Humectants like glycerin and hyaluronic acid need moisture to lock into the skin. Gently Exfoliate First (If Flaking): Never pick or tear dry flakes. Use a soft, damp washcloth in gentle circular motions to loosen dead skin before applying your balm. Use the Dab and Press Technique: Instead of aggressively dragging the tube back and forth, gently dab the product across your lips and press them together to spread it evenly without causing friction. Apply Before Lip Color: Layer your balm 5–10 minutes before applying lipstick or gloss, then gently blot off any excess. This creates a smooth canvas without affecting your lipstick's texture. Seal It Overnight: Apply a thicker layer of an occlusive balm right before bed. Your skin repairs itself while you sleep, making an overnight mask ideal for deep barrier repair. Reapply Smartly: Reapply after eating, drinking, or washing your face, and reapply SPF-infused balms every 2 hours when outdoors. Final Thoughts: Making the Best Out of Your Lip Balm Achieving soft, healthy, and hydrated lips doesn't have to be a constant struggle against the elements. By choosing a formula packed with skin-loving ingredients; like barrier-repairing ceramides, rich natural emollients, and essential SPF, you give your lips the exact support they need to stay smooth and protected all day long. While the products on this list are fantastic everyday solutions, everyone's skin is unique. If you experience chronic dryness, painful cracking, or severe sensitivities, it is always best to consult a dermatologist before introducing any new product or active ingredient into your skincare routine. A specialist can help pinpoint the root cause of your irritation and recommend a personalized care plan designed specifically for you.

title: COMSTOCK METALS BRINGS FULLY INTEGRATED INDUSTRY-SCALE SOLAR RECYCLING SYSTEM ONLINE
summary: First-of-a-Kind, 100,000-Ton-Per-Year System Successfully Processes Panels Through All Production Stages and Produces Clean, Separated Offtake Materials
body_text: First-of-a-Kind, 100,000-Ton-Per-Year System Successfully Processes Panels Through All Production Stages and Produces Clean, Separated Offtake Materials SILVER SPRINGS, NEVADA, August 11, 2026 – Comstock Inc. (NYSE: LODE) (“Comstock” and the “Company”) and Comstock Metals LLC (“Comstock Metals”), a leader in the responsible, zero-landfill recycling of end-of-life solar panels with North America’s first certified operations, announced today that Comstock Metals has fully integrated, tested and operated its complete solar panel recycling system. Comstock Metals has started its first-of-a-kind, industry-scale solar recycling facility. The system has now successfully processed panels through every stage of production, completing the final major milestone in the testing and evaluation of each unit operation. Final integration will be completed mid-August, at which point the ramp-up process to the first production milestone will begin. This milestone transitions Comstock Metals from staged equipment commissioning to full-system operations and production ramp-up. All of the facility’s processing stages have now been fully tested and connected and will be operationally integrated over the next few days. The first images in the appended video show the robotic system, feed conveyor, and particle dimensioning system in operation. This is followed by an open view of the oven system before being permanently closed; collectively representing the principal unit operations for shredding, conditioning, and other proprietary Comstock processes, and completing the start-up sequence for the 100,000-ton-per-year production line. The previously announced glass-upgrading systems have also been installed and tested ahead of the original production plan, adding expanded glass-treatment capabilities onto the original designs and supporting the production of higher-specification glass products. “We are now ready to finalize integration activities and the start of operations,” stated Corrado De Gasperis, CEO of Comstock. “Completion of the full start-up milestones brings the full production system online and demonstrates operation from panel intake through the production of final offtake materials. The team is now evaluating multiple processing scenarios and transition from commissioning to full continuous processing over the next few weeks. We anticipate reaching our first production milestone in September.” See demonstration video here of Comstock Metals’ fully integrated industry-scale system processes end-of-life solar panels from initial shredding through the production of clean, separated offtake materials. Industry-Scale Operations and Production Ramp-Up “We have now brought the industry-scale production plant online, confirmed that each stage functions as designed and to specification, and successfully stress-tested the processes at volumes representing the equipment’s stated capacities,” stated Dr. Fortunato Villamagna, President of Comstock Metals. “We are now leveraging the modular nature of the start-up process to train and develop our operating crews as we transition from a 24-hour, five-day-per-week schedule to a 24/7 schedule using 12-hour rotating shifts. These activities remain on schedule through August as we ramp toward our first production milestone of continuously operating at 25% of rated capacity.” “While our Recycling and Upgrading operations ramp up, we have also advanced the development of our proprietary Metals Recovery processes. These novel metal extraction technologies should enable the economic recovery of silver and other metals and materials from our industrial Offcut stream,” concluded Villamagna. “This work has advanced significantly over the past few months and remains on schedule toward the achievement of our next major milestone, the development of our one-ton-per-day pilot system.” About Comstock Metals Comstock Metals is a national leader in the environmentally responsible, zero-landfill recycling of end-of-life solar panels and related energy infrastructure. Comstock Metals’ internally developed recycling technologies and continuous innovation produce recovered materials that strengthen domestic supply chains for advanced technologies while helping customers eliminate the economic, environmental, and reputational liabilities associated with end-of-life panel management.
